title: They Wrote Off Ram Charan Eleven Days Ago. Now Peddi Is the Biggest South Indian Film of the Year.
excerpt: ₹393 crore and climbing, a M North American run, and a new nickname the internet won't let go of: 'Box Office Pehelwan.'
body:
Eleven days ago, the trade had its knives out. **Peddi** had opened to a thunderous ₹112 crore but slumped through the weekdays, and the whispers started early: too expensive, too slow, another **Ram Charan** swing that wouldn't connect. Janhvi Kapoor was getting trolled. The math looked grim against a breakeven north of ₹215 crore.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=noatJVfA22U</youtube>

Then the second weekend happened — and the conversation flipped entirely.

As of June 15, *Peddi* has crossed **₹393 crore worldwide** and is closing in on the ₹400 crore mark, according to the production team's own tally. More importantly, it has quietly done something no other film has managed this year: it has overtaken the Tamil juggernaut **Karuppu** to become the **highest-grossing South Indian film of 2026.** The internet, never one to miss a coronation, has already crowned Ram Charan with a new title — "Box Office Pehelwan," a nod to the wrestler-turned-everything he plays on screen.

> "Mind-blowing performance by my dear @AlwaysRamCharan. A gritty, raw performance, extraordinary body transformation, and graceful dance moves. He absolutely aced it in every aspect." — Allu Arjun

That endorsement, from Charan's own cousin and reigning Telugu box-office king, set the tone. Because *Peddi* was never really a sure thing. Directed by **Buchi Babu Sana** — the man behind the gorgeous, melancholic *Uppena* — the film asks Ram Charan to disappear into a rural sportsman across three different athletic avatars, a physical transformation that became a talking point long before the reviews landed. The gamble was whether mass Telugu audiences would follow a Mega Power Star into something this textured. They did, eventually. It just took a beat.

The numbers tell a fascinating, jagged story. *Peddi* became only the **second Ram Charan film after RRR** to cross ₹200 crore in domestic gross, and his first-ever *solo* lead film to do it — RRR, after all, had Jr NTR sharing the marquee. It's now his highest-grossing solo outing, full stop. In the elite Telugu-version club, *Peddi* sits as one of just twelve films in history to cross the ₹150 crore share mark, keeping company with *Baahubali 2*, *RRR*, *Salaar* and *Kalki 2898 AD*. That's rarefied air.

For the diaspora, the headline number is the one that matters most: *Peddi* punched through the **$3 million mark in North America** within six days, making it Ram Charan's third film to join the club after *OG* and *Mana Shankara Varaprasad Garu*. Every Tier-1 film to hit that milestone in the 2025–26 window has belonged to the Mega Family — a reminder of just how reliably this clan fills seats in Edison, Artesia and Scarborough. If you've got a Telugu-speaking household in the US, the odds are good someone already drove out to a Friday first-day-first-show.

Not that it's been a clean sweep. The trade is keeping its enthusiasm measured. *Peddi*'s recovery touched roughly 70% of breakeven by mid-run, and the weekday drops were steep enough that those early skeptics weren't entirely wrong. Insiders point out that for a film of this scale and ambition, "blockbuster" might be generous — "decent-to-strong performer" is the more honest read. The second-weekend bump (occupancy climbing back to 35% on Sunday) is what rescued the narrative, not a runaway opening.

There's also the noise around the edges. The film is reportedly being **re-edited while still in theatres** — an unusual move that goes deeper than the much-discussed trimming of Janhvi Kapoor's role. And Jagapathi Babu had to step in publicly to defend his co-star from trolls, urging audiences to remember she played exactly what the director asked of her. Star vehicles this size rarely travel without turbulence.

But milestones are milestones. Whatever the breakeven spreadsheet says, *Peddi* has restored something for Ram Charan after the back-to-back bruises of *Game Changer* and an extended *Acharya* role: the simple, unglamorous fact that he can still open and *carry* a film to the top of the year's South Indian charts. For an actor who spent the last two years being written off in certain corners, the "Box Office Pehelwan" tag isn't just a meme. It's a comeback in disguise.

*Peddi* is playing in cinemas worldwide now, with a Netflix streaming premiere expected to follow — and given the re-edit chatter, the version that lands on OTT may not be quite the one theatres got.
